explanation: G3P (glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate) is a key product of the Calvin cycle because of its chemical versatility. The hydrocarbon skeleton of G3P can be utilized by plants to synthesize a variety of crucial organic molecules. Specifically, G3P can form: fatty acids and glycerol (to make plant oils), glucose phosphate (a simple sugar), fructose (which can combine with glucose to form sucrose), storage starch, structural cellulose, and amino acids.

questions.q: Which of the following molecules CANNOT be synthesized from G3P's hydrocarbon skeleton according to the notes?
questions.exp: The notes state that G3P can form fatty acids, glycerol, glucose phosphate, fructose, starch, cellulose, and amino acids. Atmospheric nitrogen gas is inorganic and cannot be synthesized by plants.
